messages.subject: graphics help
parts:
Hi, Jeff and others:

Thank you for this fantastic package. In the past I used it a lot to
visualize and share my gene expression data. I made the images with
GDD.

Now I am trying to get it running again on a new machine with the
latest versions but I can't seem to put all the pieces together. The
machine is running Ubuntu 9.04. I've installed the latest version of
RApache and the latest (according to apt-get) libcairo2-devel and
apache. R version 2.9.1 is running. RApache works fine (at least r-
info returns a detailed page). But the graphics don't seem to work.

Here is my R script:

library(Cairo)
setContentType("image/png")
Cairo(file=stdout())
plot(rnorm(100),rnorm(100),col=2)
dev.off()
OK

Instead of a PNG I get the error
Error in Cairo(file = stdout()) :
file must be a filename. to support writing to a connection,
recompile R and Cairo with the R Connection Patch.


I can't seem to find any more information about this. Do I really need
to recompile R and Cairo? How do I get the R Connection Patch?

Thank you for your help,

Brad

The best I can recommend is to use either R compiled with cairo support
or Cairo, and you will also want to utilize the sendbin() function.

Sadly, the R Connection Patch never went anywhere with R Core simply
because it would not work across R supported platforms, e.g. Mac,
Windows, and UNIX/Linux. I hope someone can look into it and make the
necessary changes, because it would be nice to have.

Here's the sendbin.r script that you can use as a workaround (comes
bundled with rapache dist located in the test dir):

setContentType("image/png")
t <- tempfile()
png(t,type="cairo")
plot(rnorm(10))
dev.off()
sendBin(readBin(t,'raw',n=file.info(t)$size))
unlink(t)
DONE

Best,

Jeff
